title: U.S. Department of War Announces $350 Million Quantum Package, Highlighted by $150 Million OSC Loan Commitment for PsiQuantum - Quantum Computing Report
gist: The U.S. Department of War announced a $350M quantum package, including a conditional OSC loan of up to $150M to PsiQuantum for its Milpitas 'PsiFactory' and roughly $200M for DARPA QBI Stage C hardware validation. It stacks on PsiQuantum's $125M DARPA contract and $100M CHIPS award, making it the most heavily federally backed photonic FTQC player.

insights.claim: The Department of War's Office of Strategic Capital made a conditional loan commitment of up to $150 million to PsiQuantum to expand its 140,000-square-foot PsiFactory manufacturing, testing and integration hub in Milpitas, California.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Defense-backed debt (not just grants) signals the government treats photonic FTQC manufacturing as strategic industrial capacity.
insights.quote: conditional loan commitment of up to $150 million from the Department’s Office of Strategic Capital (OSC) awarded to Palo Alto-based photonic hardware developer PsiQuantum

insights.claim: The OSC loan is not final: execution depends on PsiQuantum satisfying customary legal, financial, technical and regulatory due diligence conditions.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Headline $150M is contingent; investors should not treat it as drawn capital.
insights.locator: The conditional commitment from the OSC

insights.claim: The OSC financing is earmarked for capex on hardware validation equipment, subassembly integration infrastructure and advanced cryogenic systems for large-scale photonic prototype testing.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Points to demand for cryogenic and test-equipment suppliers tied to photonic QC scale-up.
insights.locator: The conditional commitment from the OSC

insights.claim: PsiQuantum has accumulated a run of public awards in 2026: a $125 million expanded DARPA QBI contract in July and a definitive $100 million CHIPS and Science Act award in September, now followed by the up-to-$150M OSC loan.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Roughly $375M of US public money in a quarter makes PsiQuantum a de facto national champion, de-risking its funding runway.
insights.locator: The OSC commitment follows a series

insights.claim: PsiQuantum is building utility-scale sites in parallel on two continents: Moreton Bay Central in Queensland, Australia and an anchor site at the Illinois Quantum and Microelectronics Park in Chicago.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Multi-site buildout implies heavy capex burn that public debt and grants are increasingly underwriting.

themes.theme: DARPA QBI Stage C shifts to physical testing

insights.claim: About $200 million of the $350 million package goes to new DARPA Quantum Benchmarking Initiative Stage C commitments across selected industry performers.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Stage C selection is a key credibility filter for quantum hardware companies competing for government validation.

insights.claim: QBI Stage C moves evaluation from theoretical blueprint audits to physical hardware testing to verify whether candidate utility-scale designs can actually be built as specified.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Physical IV&V will expose which FTQC roadmaps are real, a potential catalyst for winners and losers among listed quantum names.
insights.quote: Stage C transitions evaluation from theoretical blueprint audits to physical hardware testing to verify whether candidate utility-scale concepts can be built as designed

themes.theme: Defense demand-side and supply chain sovereignty

insights.claim: R&E and DARPA will co-host application workshops starting before January 2027 with DOE, NNSA and the Laboratory for Physical Sciences to identify mission-critical quantum use cases in chemistry, materials science and physics.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Defense agencies are building the demand side for FTQC, not just funding supply.

insights.claim: A stated aim of the package is securing domestic supply chain capacity for assembly, testing and validation of components underpinning fault-tolerant quantum computing.
insights.speaker: Mohamed Abdel-Kareem
insights.so_what: Onshoring of quantum supply chains is becoming explicit defense policy, favoring US-based manufacturers.
